# Independent ICP cycle-budget reconciliation

## Result
The Figure 5A processing workbook implies less cumulative recovered Li under pulsed operation over the ten recorded cycles: 10.2573839662 versus 12.7700421941 in the workbook’s formula-implied mg/g units for CC, ratio 0.8032380638. This is a workbook-derived, ten-cycle net-recovery comparison with unresolved dilution and inventory factors; absolute mg/g values are not independently validated. It is not a validated lifetime yield, measured electrode-life endpoint, or equal-clock-time throughput comparison.

The same workbook reproduces the paper's capacity retention: 32.7453142% pulse versus 13.1384160% CC. Both divide cycle 10 by each mode's own cycle 1. Pulse begins with a smaller recovery increment. Pulse exceeds CC in individual cycles 6–10 but has not caught up cumulatively by cycle 10.

## Source and methods
Public sources: https://zenodo.org/records/23064370 and https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.6c04447 . Original workbook paths relative to this directory: `figure 05/raw data/Li uptake experiments/Figure 5A/processing.xlsx` (Sheet2) and matching `raw data.xlsx` (Sheet1). No workbook was changed. Primary-runtime Python/openpyxl was used read-only. Newly authored extraction/reconciliation code is `reconcile_icp.py`; auditable extracted cells and results are `icp_cycle_reconciliation.json`.

Processing D3,D5,...,D21 use (B_odd−B_previous)*0.1/0.158. J3,J5,...,J21 use the corresponding H cells. D23=D21*100/D3 and J23=J21*100/J3. Raw headers identify ppm; sample labels identify recovery solution at 0 and 0.5 h, not feed depletion. Raw Mean cells reconcile the processing concentration values except the discrepancies below. Each instrument measurement also has numbered readings and SD/RSD. These must not be counted as independent electrode experiments.

# Lithium recovery transition: a finite physical opportunity and a rest-control no-go

16 October 2026. Independent capability-first worker. Read-only knowledge checkout: `/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/ultra/work/astra-positive-memory-20261016`, supplied pin `f937563cbc5d2249b8e0dd96bcbd3b8f78eb85c6` (no Git command used to verify it). Original handoff files were read without modification. No peer-worker output, external contact, install, hardware job, or nested delegation was used.

## Decision

**The supplied measurements do not identify a new species-aware rest controller or a lifetime-yield winner.** The strongest actionable opportunity found is to collect and characterize the presently unaccounted feed-to-rinse-to-recovery liquid, then retain only qualified fractions. The proposed capture schedule is the published P4–8 incumbent. This shifts the target from inventing another pulse shape to obtaining additional isolated source lithium at the recovery boundary.

The physical change is modest: an outlet fraction collector or equal-backpressure diverter, isolated collection bottles, complete liquid accounting, and offline elemental/isotopic assays. A conserved isotope budget can identify a lower bound on new source lithium even when isotope fractionation is not assumed absent. No such run or useful wash-fraction yield is present in the acquired records. The primitive and fractionation methods have prior art; historical originality and practical advantage of this combination remain **UNKNOWN**.

## Primary-source findings that change the opportunity

The [2026 ACS paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.6c04447), Experimental §2.4 and Results §§3.3–3.4, specifies a 15-minute DI-water flush between capture and release into a LiCl receiver. It already optimizes four-second pulses across 1, 4, 8, and 12-second rests, selects P4–8, and tests reverse-pulse operation without a noticeable improvement over pulse/rest. Its discussion treats the reduction at twelve seconds as a possible mechanism. It reports better own-initial retention after ten cycles. The paper does not provide a complete wash-stream inventory or its disposition. These observations make wash collection a separate intervention and prevent presenting longer rest or reverse pulses as a new primitive. # Conserved-isotope product certificate

Newly authored, 16 October 2026. This is elementary conservation/partial identification applied to a proposed chemical measurement. It is not an experimentally calibrated model and carries no historical novelty claim.

## 1. Exact one-pool identified interval

Fix a complete control volume and a finite time horizon. Every lithium atom entering it is classified by origin as source-feed or nonfeed. Origin persists through exchange, dissolution, isotope fractionation, and reintercalation. Let i be 6Li or 7Li. Assume:

- Total source input of isotope i is a_i >= 0.
- Total nonfeed input of isotope i is bounded by b_i >= 0.
- A physically isolated deliverable product pool, after assay aliquots and any finishing/storage losses, contains z_i >= 0 atoms/moles of isotope i.
- No undeclared source, nuclear isotope conversion, or inaccessible initial store can supply that isotope.
- Unretained outputs/stores are unrestricted except for nonnegative inventories. Additional real constraints can only tighten the result.

Let f_i denote source-origin isotope i in the product. Necessarily

```
0 <= f_i <= a_i,
0 <= z_i - f_i <= b_i.
```

Therefore

```
l_i = max(0, z_i - b_i) <= f_i <= u_i = min(z_i, a_i).
```

If l_i > u_i, the inputs and observed pool are inconsistent with the declared budgets. Fail the premise; do not clip the contradiction into an apparent result.

Conversely, for any f_i in [l_i,u_i], put f_i source atoms and z_i-f_i nonfeed atoms in the product. Put all remaining source atoms and any remaining nonfeed atoms in unobserved allowed stores/outputs. All inventories are nonnegative. Thus the interval is sharp given exactly this one-pool, conservation-only information. If b_i is only an upper bound, choose a feasible actual nonfeed input at most b_i. The construction is an identifiability witness, not a proposed chemical mechanism.

The two isotope allocations are independent under these minimal premises, so total source lithium F=f_6+f_7 has the sharp interval

```
L = max(0,z_6-b_6) + max(0,z_7-b_7),
U = min(z_6,a_6) + min(z_7,a_7).
```
